long_biography.plain_text:
The Grace Center for Innovation in Nursing Education carries the name of Charlene Edson's mother, Grace Converse, who worked as a nurse. The simulation facility emerged from a wider Edson family gift intended to strengthen clinical teaching. Its focus reflects Edson's own experience in the profession and her concern for compassionate care.

A separate part of the gift funded research into dementia, along with tools for patients and family caregivers. Edson later broadened that work with Grant Simpson by backing fellowships for advanced practitioners in neurology and memory care. Through supervised clinical training, the program prepares specialists to support families facing cognitive illness. Her service with the Quiet Heart Foundation provides another channel for charitable grants to education, health and community organisations.
